request.prompt: Create a strong HAVENLINE World 1 purchase-value upgrade concept sheet, using the supplied references as the retained base identity and scale anchors. Chunky rounded stylized 3D mobile-game art: warm orange timber, deep blue painted metal, rounded gray hardware and softly sculpted snow. Clean navy studio ground, controlled lighting and clear silhouettes. The upgrades must visibly add working structure and a useful operation, not just thicker brackets or a recolor. Make EXACTLY two rows by three roomy columns, six substantial panels. Top row is the first new proposal; bottom row is the later new proposal. Within each row show the SAME physical design in exterior front three-quarter, genuine opposite rear three-quarter, and an open/cutaway functional view. Keep a consistent scale and physical coordinate system within each row. The functional view is the same object with roof/guard hidden, never an extra design. Preserve approved ordinary resource size and standard conveyor width/height. Bigger buildings and new ports are authored upgrades with clear purchased ground area, not enlarged resources or a new belt skin. Do not show the old base as a newly designed third stage. Titles and short stage/view labels only; no numerical levels, prices, yields, capacity or rate claims. Footer: AUTHORED UPGRADE PROPOSAL. No workers, UI, magic energy, electric fields or unsupported fuel system. This is proposed design, not proof of runtime implementation. HEADER: HAVENLINE / STORAGE HOUSE PROGRESSION. Existing references already have typed organization; the new purchase value must be visibly larger physical workflow. TOP ROW label DISPATCH WAREHOUSE. Preserve a recognizable central timber house with blue roof and central front blue sliding doors, then add a substantial left receiving wing with its own covered unloading apron. Add a separate front-left dispatch canopy and clearly distinct physical reserved-order staging racks. Keep a broad unobstructed central pedestrian aisle and the isolated right-side fuel hatch. Goods enter from the object LEFT wing and depart at the separate FRONT-LEFT dispatch hatch in the new wing; the original central front doors remain clear; these positions do not mirror between views. BOTTOM ROW label LOGISTICS HALL. Make a decisive larger twin-gable warehouse with stone lower protection, blue frames, tall typed racks, separate covered receiving and dispatch bays, a practical hand-operated gantry/hoist over a loading cradle and an open pedestrian corridor. The original house facade remains recognizable in the central core. Receiving is at the object left/rear bay, dispatch at the front/left bay, fuel service at the right exterior hatch; leave separate outside aprons for each and no crossing through the central pedestrian aisle. Shutters and low protective walls must not seal the working doors. In the third panel of each row remove the near roof plane to show the SAME interior: receiving stock, typed holding racks, reserved dispatch staging and clear aisle must connect physically. Put a few correctly scaled representative material/food/timber/fuel bundles in distinct bays, with food storage only and fuel apart. Show storage containers and a loading cradle, not giant decorative resource piles. No people or vehicle required; keep space for ordinary workers and approved conveyor interfaces; do not depict or imply a direct truck-unloading bay. Short view captions FRONT / REAR / CUTAWAY. No cash generation, food-processing machinery, magical conveyor-through-wall connection or numerical storage labels. The original central front sliding-door opening and its entire pedestrian aisle must remain unblocked; dispatch uses its own front-left hatch, not that opening. Draw separate receiving, accepted typed stock and reserved outgoing physical zones without multiplying the same goods. Only worker or compatible standard conveyor handoffs; no direct truck unloading at this building.
